title: A bailar
theme: Four dances, placed symmetrically: TANGO, CORRIDO, MILONGA, SALSA. Straight clues; one wordplay clue (37A).

clues.16A: Tropezones que acaban en el suelo

clues.24A: Baile rioplatense y lugar donde se baila
clues.35A: Como las líneas que venden vuelos
clues.37A: ¿Ritmo caribeño que se sirve en la mesa?

unsure.MILONGA: List score 47 (rare in the frequency data) but a real, well-known word; it is a theme entry.
unsure.CORRIDO: The Mexican song form: a genre more than a dance, so the 'four dances' label is loose.
unsure.CAIDAS: Falls: checked against the content rule, clued lightly.
unsure.CASADA: Clue assumes 'sí, quiero' (the wedding answer in Spain; Latin America often says 'sí, acepto').
unsure.ILUSOS: Fine as a word; the clue is a little loose.
unsure.AMORES / AMAS: Not forms of one word (amor, ama), so the rule passes, but both come from amar. AMAS is clued as the noun 'dueñas'. A strict editor may still want one of them gone.
unsure.SUBIRA / ORA / SACA / LEO: Conjugations; all common forms. Only SUBIRA cannot be read as anything else.
unsure.EROS: A proper name from mythology, as fill.

build: findSkeleton with seeds MILONGA, CORRIDO, SALSA, TANGO at floor 52: five of six random seeds gave a skeleton (20 to 25 blocks); this one has 21.
Three curation rounds of 400 to 500 fills at floor 52 (174 to 411 distinct each), ranked by disliked words, same-root pairs and entries below 50.

Lower-left corner refilled three times. First at floor 52 (6 distinct) to remove OLER beside OLORES and AMAMOS beside AMAS; then at floor 50 with ORAL rejected, because the 15×15 needs ORAL, which left AMABAS in 19D beside AMAS. On 2026-11-13, with the rebuilt engine and the same-root rule: 1,500 fills at floor 50 with every form of amar rejected gave 6 clean grids; this one (AMORES, PICARO, COLOSO, APICE, OCULAR) keeps ILUSOS and SOSO at list score 50 to 52.
